**TL;DR**

- **Index-level loss, breadth-level gain.** S&P 500 −0.57%, Nasdaq Composite −2.00%, Dow −0.85%, but Russell 2000 **+1.29%** and 9 of 11 S&P sectors higher.
- 2,301 of 4,151 matched US names rose (median **+0.40%**). This was a mega-cap-tech de-rating, not a broad risk-off week.
- **The AI-returns reckoning.** Alphabet −12.6% Thu (worst day since its 2004 listing, ~$500bn of market cap, Q3 capex $51.4bn, FCF negative a second quarter), Amazon −1.4% Fri ($42.4bn TTM FCF deficit), Intel **−28.58%** Fri (Q4 guide $15–16bn vs $17.1bn consensus;
- worst day since 1974). Nasdaq-100 on pace for a >$1trn one-day value loss.
- **Rotation, not retreat.** XLC −5.32% and XLK −2.03% were the only losing sector ETFs. XLV +3.12%, XLB +2.79%, XLU +2.04%, XLY +2.02%, XLI +1.69%.
- Health care hit a record high Friday; Exxon and Chevron touched records on refining margins.
- **A hawkish Fed that did not hike.** FOMC held 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in a **10–2 vote** — Cook and Hammack dissented *for a 25bp hike* —
- in Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair. Q3 GDP +3.4% ann. (cons 3.1%); Sept PCE +0.5% m/m, 3.6% y/y (from 3.4%). December 9 hike odds ~75–85%.
- 10-year fell ~6bp to 4.93% — safe-haven demand, not a dovish repricing.
- **Week ahead is dense.** US midterm elections Tue Nov 3, ISM Mfg Mon, JOLTS Tue, ADP + ISM Services Wed, claims/productivity Thu, **October payrolls Fri** (consensus +55k to +75k;
- prior +29k; U/E 4.2%), plus Apple, Palantir, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm and Berkshire. Six Fed officials speak. RBA decision Mon, BoE Thu. OPEC meeting.
- **Tail risks live off the tape.** $6.3bn Binance hack hit crypto-linked equities (COIN −15.3% wk, CRCL −17.4%);
- WTI >$104 with Iran conflict unresolved (Trump waiting until after the midterms for new military action); gold −2.7% to $3,899 on Fed-hike fear.

**4. Recap — Themes of the week**

- **AI spending must now show a return.** Anthropic's S-1 filing on Monday briefly lifted the trade;
- by Friday the market was repricing the capex-to-cash-flow bridge across the megacaps (GOOGL capex $51.4bn and a second negative-FCF quarter;
- AMZN's TTM FCF outflow >$42bn and a Q4 revenue guide below expectations; INTC's guide). Nasdaq-100 was on course for its steepest one-day value loss since mid-June (>$1trn).
- **Rotation out of megacap tech into everything else.** Nine of eleven S&P sectors up; Russell 2000 outperformed a third straight week; health care and energy at records;
- staples, utilities and materials bid as the safe-haven bid showed up in bonds (10y below 4.95%) rather than in the index.
- **A hawkish Fed that paused — and oil on top of it.** Warsh's first FOMC held at 3.75–4.00% with two dissents *for a hike*;
- Q3 GDP +3.4% and PCE 3.6% y/y kept December hike odds at ~75–85%.
- WTI above $100 (Iran conflict unresolved) kept an energy-inflation impulse in the data; on Friday, Musalem and Barkin both argued rates need to rise.
- **Private capital re-rating cash-flow stories.** ADT's $10/share cash take-private (+45.6% premium, ~9.5x EV/FCF on the $15.3bn EV) is the week's clearest signal that cheap, asset-heavy, cash-generative listed companies are being re-rated by sponsors.
- **Crypto's Binance shock.** A reported $6.3bn Binance theft hit crypto-linked equities (COIN −15.3% wk, CRCL −17.4%, MSTR/RIOT lower) and BTC −4.78%.
- **Post-earnings dispersion inside health care.** The sector ETF made a record high while Alnylam fell 26% and Sprouts 26% on guidance and comps —
- the tape rewarded *large* health-care names and punished execution slips.

**9. Forward preview — Themes traders are positioning for**

- **"Show the return on the capex" continues.** Apple, Palantir and AMD now inherit an earnings bar defined by Alphabet, Amazon and Intel:
- revenue is no longer enough, free cash flow and backlog quality are the test.
- Any further downgrade to AI-adjacent revenue multiples pressures QQQ again; any evidence of capex→cash-flow conversion repairs it.
- **Breadth > index.** With 2,301 of 4,151 names up and small caps +1.29%, the market is already paying for rotation.
- The risk is that a payrolls surprise re-concentrates flows back into the megacaps.
- **A policy-risk overlay.** Midterms on Tuesday (polls show Democrats with a shot at both chambers) raise the odds of scrutiny of data-center permitting and crypto/bank regulation;
- defense and drug-pricing policy are the two live sensitivities. Consensus is that election results alone will move less than earnings and payrolls.
- **Oil is the hawkish tail.** WTI above $104 with the Iran situation unresolved and OPEC meeting this week means a supply headline is a rate-hike headline.
- Friday's safe-haven rally in bonds only held because AI names were being sold; an oil spike plus a hot CPI would remove that offset.
- **Private-market re-rating of cash generators.** ADT's take-private opened a bid for asset-heavy, low-growth, high-FCF names (the stock's own EV/FCF of ~9.5x and equity-only ~4.7x are the tell).
- Named candidates in the week's mover set: FDXF, SGRY, HAYW, RKT.
